sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Round each factor to the nearest ten to estimate 47 × 62.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A student says 5112 - 2112 = 3000. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3000 and the rounded estimate is 3000.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 3000.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3100 and the rounded estimate is 3000.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 3100.

items.prompt: A student evaluates [62 + 14] × 9 - 10: “They multiply 14 by 9 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 178.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student multiplied before evaluating [62 + 14]; the grouped sum is 76, giving 674.
The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 675.
The work is correct; 178 is the value.
The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 676.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 9576644, the value of the 4 in the ones place is 10 times as much as the value of the 4 in the tens place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 4 and 40; 4 is 1/10 as much as 40, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The values are 4 and 40; 4 is 10 times as much as 40, so the student's comparison is correct.
The values are 4 and 40; 4 is 10 times as much as 40.
The places are adjacent, so 4 is 100 times as much as 40.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Subtract 3 from 7, multiply the difference by 4, then add 41.”
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
